title: Variance-aware key shaping and staged TTL rollback procedures
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: produce a prescriptive, automated flow for KV/prefix caching changes that combines a variance-aware hit-rate model, conservative TTL tuning heuristics, safe staged apply (shadow -> canary -> gradual), and deterministic rollback gates. Deliverables: (1) hit-rate estimator that accounts for prefix variance and sequence length skew, (2) key-shaping recommendations to reduce fragmentation for common low-entropy prefixes, (3) TTL tuning rules that trade hit-rate vs staleness with explicit cost delta projections, (4) a staged apply orchestration integrated with rollouts that uses shadow traffic and statistical safety tests to automatically halt/rollback on regressions, (5) a simulation harness and dashboard for forecasting cost and latency impact before apply.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hit-rate estimator PR merged + unit tests and bench results demonstrating within +/-5% of observed hit-rate on 3 sampled workloads; 2) Key-shaping rule set committed and config UI schema defined; 3) TTL tuning policy library with rollback thresholds implemented in the rollout engine; 4) End-to-end canary flow that performs shadow validation, required safety checks (p99 latency, downstream error rate, hit-rate delta), and automatic rollback when thresholds exceeded; 5) Simulation notebooks and dashboard panels available and documented in Confluence.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket. Collected prior artifacts: sampling notebook (drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kv-sampling-2024), prefix taxonomy doc (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/KV+Prefix+Taxonomy). Proposed a variance-aware model that weights per-prefix entropy and sequence-length distribution.

2025-02-18 - Rohan Patel: Spiked on estimator; prototype algorithm uses moving-window prefix hit estimator + Bayesian shrinkage for low-observation prefixes. Bench against traffic from prod-shadow month of Jan; results in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-tools/pull/187. Observed that some customer-heavy prefixes show multi-modal hit curves -> need cluster-aware key shaping.

2025-02-22 - Mei Chen (PM): Reviewed initial approach. Concern: TTL reduction could increase downstream model cost in edge cases. Action: add a cost-safety gate that projects token-cost delta over a 24h window and requires approval if > 5% increase for affected customer group.

2025-02-25 - Design review (Don Ruiz): UX spec for rollout controls v1 uploaded: https://figma.com/file/kv-rollout-ui. Suggests exposing estimated token-savings and worst-case rollback reason in the console during staging.

2025-02-28 - Rohan Patel: Integration notes - implemented staged apply steps: shadow-run for 1 hour, canary to 5% traffic for 12h, ramp to 50% over 48h. Safety checks run at 5m intervals; stop-and-rollback if hit-rate drop > 6% AND p99 latency increase > 30ms OR downstream error rate increase > 0.1%. Added a secondary check that requires 3 consecutive failing intervals before automated rollback to avoid flapping.

2025-03-01 - Security (Priya Singh): Confirmed no sensitive customer keys logged by the simulation harness. Security review not required for this change but recommend audit logging for TTL changes. See ticket SEC-483 for audit-logging plan.

2025-03-02 - Rohan Patel: PR for rollout orchestration and policy library opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/402. Added unit tests for safety gate evaluation and canary metrics. Next: add platform dashboard panels and run 72h shadow validation on staging traffic (blocked until staging capacity available).
risks: 1) Misestimation of hit-rate for low-sample prefixes causing cost regressions. 2) Rollout flapping leading to delayed applies. 3) Interactions between key-shaping and downstream analytics that rely on original keys. Mitigations: Bayesian shrinkage, conservative staging windows, and a compatibility mode that preserves canonical key mapping for analytics export.
next_steps: 1) Get staging capacity for 72h shadow run (ops ticket OP-872). 2) Wire dashboard panels for cost projection and rollback reasons. 3) Run canary on a low-risk customer cohort and validate cost and latency projections. 4) Postmortem template for any rollback events.
notes: This ticket intentionally targets a conservative first-cut: favor safety and observability over aggressive TTL reduction. Longer term follow-ups will include automated key-canonicalization transforms and per-tenant policy tuning.
